items.title: Sherlock Bones and the Mystery in the Meadow
items.body:
When a mysterious “murder” is discovered in the meadow, detectives must examine clues and determine what happened. This mystery is an interactive animal- tracking and murder mystery program that combines nature exploration, forensic investigation, and problem solving. Participants will become wildlife detectives along with Sherlock Bones, a clever detective who specializes in animal tracks, skulls, and bones. Follow the tracks. Study the bones! Solve the mystery with the Missouri Department of Conservation!

register

items.title: The Science and Art of Soap Making- Session 2
items.body:
Making soap is fun and can be educational. It’s chemistry, art, and nature all in one! Discover how early Missouri pioneers made soap using the ash from hardwood trees and their fires and the fat from their butchered animals with the Missouri Department of Conservation. Don’t worry if you are squeamish! We will use modern-day ingredients to make soap you can take home and use (Lard with some oils, Lye, and Distilled Water). We will go over the science behind soap, how its connected to conservation, and the importance of safety using the ingredients and additives.

You MUST attend one of two virtual presentations in order to make soap on 11/21 due to the nature of this program and safety. After both virtual sessions, you will get an email to pick one of the in-person sessions on 11/21 either 10am-1pm (20 spots) or 3-6pm (20 spots). Participants will work in groups of 4 to complete step-by-step instructions and each person will take home their own bars of soap.

Ages 16 and up

items.title: Dutch Oven Friendsgiving (CANCELLED)
items.body:
This program has been cancelled. We apologize for any inconvinence.

Experience a Friendsgiving meal prepared the old-fashioned way— over hot coals! In this program with the Missouri Department of Conservation, discover the basics of Dutch oven cooking including care and regulating temperature, as well as other helpful tips and tricks. Friends will help prepare a complete holiday feast outdoors, including an appetizer, main dish, and dessert. Then we’ll enjoy the feast together!

This hands-on program is perfect for anyone wanting to try outdoor cooking, spend quality time or meet new friends, and enjoy a hearty meal in nature. All materials and ingredients are provided.

This program will take place completely outside, so dress for the weather and bring your own beverages.

This program is for adults 18+. Please register EACH person who will be present to ensure we purchase enough food for everyone.

items.title: Walk Before Work Club
items.body:
Photography by Kari R. Frey, FREYtography

Start your day off with movement and join the Missouri Department of Conservation at Tower Grove Park for a walk before work! We'll meet at the Roman Pavilion and go on a short 45-minute walk through the park, learning a little about the plants and animals along the way. We'll end promptly at 7:30 am, so everyone can get to work on time.

items.title: Gaddy Wild Bird Garden Volunteer Training
items.body:
This training is for those interested in joining Tower Grove Park's new ongoing team, Gaddy Wild Bird Garden Volunteer Group.

Welcome to the Gaddy Wild Bird Garden Volunteer Group and thank you for your interest in assisting Tower Grove Park’s forestry team in managing this important bird habitat area. The Gaddy Wild Bird Garden is a natural area encompassing approximately 1.48 acres in the northwest area of Tower Grove Park; this area has been designated as an Important Bird Area by the National Audubon Society, and more than 200 resident and migratory bird species have been recorded within the Garden. TGP’s Forestry Team is training volunteers to help park staff achieve management goals and improve this habitat area. TGP Forestry will be hosting multiple training sessions throughout the summer and fall to prepare for working days during the dormant season. Training sessions will be hands-on and will focus on multiple aspects of park and habitat management.

items.title: Homeschool Program: Living Harmony (CANCELLED)
items.body:
This program has been cancelled due to insufficient registrants. We apologize for the inconvenience.


This program is for homeschooling groups and families only.

There are countless interactions between plants, animals, and people every day at Tower Grove Park. How does nature strike a balance? Using dramatic play, animal artifacts, and an Osage Culture Traveling Trunk, let's observe these interactions up close at the Park's East Stream (Nee Kee Nee). Together, we will learn about indigenous connections with flora and fauna and discuss how we still depend on each other today.

This homeschooling program is presented jointly with Tower Grove Park's Education Team and the Missouri Department of Conservation.

This program is for kindergarten through 4th grade.

Learn more about our homeschooling programs by visiting towergrovepark.org/homeschool

Registration Opens: October 15th, 10 am

Registration Closes: November 11th, 10 am

items.title: Tree Sucker Removal Training
items.body:
The goal of the tree sucker removal volunteer group is to assist the Tower Grove Park Forestry Department in maintaining a clean, manicured aesthetic throughout the arboretum by pruning low sucker (epicormic) growth from trees. Epicormic growth occurs when dormant buds emerge due to stressors such as drought, soil compaction, wounding, construction disturbance, or as part of the natural growth habit of certain tree and shrub species. Regardless of the cause, Tower Grove Park routinely removes sucker growth to preserve plant health and park appearance.

Volunteers will be trained to understand and identify sucker growth, safely and properly use pruning tools including hand pruners, loppers, and hand saws, and sanitize tools to prevent the spread of plant pathogens. Training sessions, led by Forestry Supervisor Joseph Hart, will include access to the volunteer toolbox, an overview of available tools, and instruction on using GIS and the park’s mapping software to assign work areas. The group will then move into the park for hands-on training, beginning with a demonstration followed by supervised practice removing sucker growth from multiple trees.

At the conclusion of the training, there will be time for discussion and guidance on working independently throughout the growing season. After completing training, volunteers will receive an interactive map with assigned work areas.

Participants are invited to join an optional two-hour tree sucker removal session once a month with Joseph and his forestry team.

Volunteers without smartphone or web access will need to coordinate directly with Joseph prior to working.

items.title: Osage Culture Traveling Trunk presented by Tower Grove Park
items.body:
Join Tower Grove Park staff at Carpenter Library to view the Osage Culture Traveling Trunk. This trunk is designed to educate young Missourians about the Osage people who lived in Missouri when Europeans first arrived. The Traveling Trunk contains Osage Nation approved materials about Osage history, language, and culture. The main goal of the trunk is to foster an understanding of Osage culture and heritage throughout ancestral Osage territory in Missouri.

This resource is designed for elementary through middle school students, as well as interested high school students and adults.

Learn more

items.title: TGFM Off-Season Market
items.body:
Off-Season Markets at Tower Grove Park

We stay in the park ALL YEAR LONG! 🌳 Join us at Tower Grove Park on the 1st and 3rd Saturdays of each month, November through March, for our off-season markets. Follow us on Instagram for updates and check out the full schedule below!

OFF-SEASON MARKETS

  • When: 1st and 3rd Saturdays of the month

  • Where: Tower Grove Park

  • November–December: 9 a.m.–1 p.m.

WINTER MARKET

  • When: 1st and 3rd Saturdays of the month

  • Where: Tower Grove Park

  • January–March 2027: 10 a.m.–1 p.m.

items.title: You and Me under the Canopy: Salamander Shuffle!
items.body:
Do your little ones enjoy being in nature? Appreciate the natural world through a story, songs, movement, and play as you sit under the canopy for a “nature” adventure. Come see the topic the Missouri Department of Conservation is exploring this month, the fall migration and life cycle of salamanders in Missouri! Younger children and siblings are welcome. Meet the naturalist at the Stupp Center as we will be indoors but will have an activity outside; weather permitting.

items.title: Bug Lab- Session 2
items.body:
Learn the exciting and valuable jobs insects have while interacting with living animals. This program by the Missouri Botanical Garden’s Sophia M. Sachs Butterfly House uses both mounted and living insects to give your students insights into the roles insects play in our world. This program features our largest variety of living animals, and each animal reveals the stories of how insects find food, escape danger, benefit other living things, and more!

All individuals will need to register, including any adults who will be in attendance.

Registration will open 4 weeks prior to program date.
